output.summary: NOV reported revenues of $1.25 billion and a net loss of $115 million for the first quarter of 2021, with consolidated revenue declining 6% sequentially due to ongoing customer austerity, operational disruptions from severe weather, and pandemic-related supply chain issues. EBITDA fell to breakeven, prompting further cost reductions. Despite these challenges, NOV observed early signs of recovery in the oilfield, especially in Wellbore Technologies and North America, where demand for products like drill bits, downhole tools, and inspection services rose sharply. The company reduced costs by $12.6 billion since 2014 and achieved $52 million in annualized cost savings during the quarter, projecting $106 million in total 2021 savings. NOV ended the quarter with $1.61 billion in cash and $1.85 billion in gross debt, having redeemed $183 million in senior notes. The Wellbore Technologies segment generated $413 million in revenue (up 11% sequentially) with EBITDA of $34 million and expects 8-10% sequential growth in Q2. The Completion & Production Solutions segment reported $439 million in revenue (down 20% sequentially), an EBITDA loss of $4 million, and a book-to-bill of 127%. It anticipates 15-25% sequential revenue improvement in Q2. The Rig Technologies segment generated $431 million in revenue (down 1% sequentially) with EBITDA of $13 million and a book-to-bill of 59%. The segment initiated manufacturing from its new Saudi Arabia plant and is pursuing over $400 million in offshore wind projects. NOV expressed cautious optimism for the remainder of 2021, citing signs of recovery, improved pricing, and growing customer demand in select markets.
